text: Much of AI's value comes from its ability to work autonomously or semi-autonomously. Microsoft 365 Copilot offers a simple way to start automating repetitive work with scheduled prompts. You can schedule tasks like daily briefings, weekly summaries, or meeting preparation without building a complex automation. At the scheduled time, Copilot runs your prompt automatically and generates a response for you to review. And because you're using Microsoft 365 Copilot, it can also draw on relevant work context, such as emails, meetings, and chats, depending on your permissions and organization's settings. Let's see how it works. First, I open Copilot Chat and sign in with my Microsoft 365 work account. Make sure WorkIQ is turned on. Otherwise, you won't see the scheduled prompt option. Now, I enter the task I want Copilot to repeat. For example, review the past week's news about the consulting industry and give me a five-bullet executive brief focused on implications for leaders. Keep it under 200 words. Or, using my work context, I could ask Copilot to give me an overview of today's meetings and how to prepare for each one. Once Copilot responds, I hover over my original prompt, click the clock icon, and select Schedule this prompt. Here, I can define when and how often the prompt should run. I'll set mine to every Monday at 8am. I can also choose an end date and turn on email notifications when a new response is ready. I'd recommend keeping notifications on so you don't miss the results. Then, I click Save. That's it! Copilot will now run the prompt automatically according to my schedule. When Copilot runs the prompt, the result appears in my regular chats area marked as a scheduled conversation. To manage my schedules, I open Settings and More, then select Scheduled Prompts. Here, I can see all my active schedules. I can select Run Now to trigger a prompt immediately, edit its schedule, turn it off, or delete it. So, as my needs change, I can adjust the schedule or improve the prompt rather than starting from scratch. Think about the tasks you repeat every week. You might use Scheduled Prompts for a daily meeting briefing, a summary of important emails, regular project check-ins, or a weekly leadership update. Just remember that Scheduled Prompts require an eligible Microsoft 365 Copilot license. They're available in supported Copilot Chat, Teams, and Outlook Experiences on web and desktop, depending on your organization's settings. And, as always, review important AI-generated information before acting on it. The key shift is moving from manually asking AI for the same information every time to having AI perform recurring work for you automatically.
